title: Key-tenant verification needs the `sessions` scope on the tick's key (GET /webinar-operations); a least-privilege tick key (gmail + calendar) is always `tenant-unverified` once enforcement is enabled
evidence: X-LKB-Tenant is set only by GET /webinar-operations (requireScope sessions). The tick calls /meeting-candidates (gmail) and /calendar/upcoming (calendar); neither sets the header. A key without sessions gets 403, so unknown, so tenant-unverified: fail-closed schedules nothing, fail-open leaves the selection unchanged with a warning.
fix_direction: Operator: grant `sessions` to the tick's key before enabling, OR API change (1 line): res.setHeader('X-LKB-Tenant', req.auth.tenantId) in the GET /meeting-candidates handler, then point KEY_TENANT_PATH there (removes the extra request). Approver/operator decision; high at enablement.

title: The tenant signal rides on GET /webinar-operations, whose handler answers 503 (and sets NO X-LKB-Tenant) whenever the webinar operations state file is oversize, malformed or ownership-invalid: under fail-closed an unrelated state-file fault stops ALL recording, as tenant-unverified
evidence: listWebinarOperations throws for a >5 MiB data/webinar-release/operations.json, a non-object state, an invalid state.tenantId or malformed discovery health; the route catches and returns 503 'operation_state_unavailable' without the header (header is set only on the 200 path). The tick maps any non-OK status to null => tenant-unverified => fail-closed skips every item rules-unevaluable. A missing file or another tenant's file is fine (200 with header). Read from the code; not run against the real API (no DB). Also: the handler reads and parses the file (up to 5 MiB, synchronous readFileSync/JSON.parse) and serialises the operations list on every enforcing tick (every 5 min) only for a header; there is no cheaper existing form (Express serves HEAD through the same GET handler).
fix_direction: Same fix as ISS-TENANTSIG-001(b): set X-LKB-Tenant from req.auth.tenantId on GET /meeting-candidates (a route the tick already calls under its own key, no state file, scope gmail) and point KEY_TENANT_PATH there; the extra request and this coupling both disappear. Until then the operator must treat a fail-closed total stop with 'GET /webinar-operations -> 503' in the log as an operations-state problem, not a tenant problem.
regression_check: none yet; after the API change: tick test that a 503 on the verification route is not reachable (route is /meeting-candidates)
